> Generalist, project-agnostic. Project identity is read from
> `.ssot/context-index.md` and `.ssot/agents/clients.json` at runtime.
> ## You are in an ACOS project
> ACOS maintains a single source of truth under `.ssot/` and projects it to
> multiple AI clients. You are one of those clients.
> ## Orientation sequence (read before acting)
> 1. **Project identity** — `.ssot/context-index.md` (name, role, specs, sources)
> 2. **Current state** — `.ssot/status.md` (objective, milestone, open items)
> 3. **Next action** — `.ssot/handoff.md` (recommended next action)
> 4. **Ecosystem** — if `clients.json` declares `ecosystemParent`, read parent
>    `.ssot/context-index.md` and `.ssot/status.md`
> 5. **Authority** — `.ssot/protected-paths.json` (edit vs managed)
> 6. **Entry points** — context-index "Common entrypoints" = command surface
> 7. **Prefix standardization** — before adding a custom entrypoint, check whether the need is
>    already covered by a core category in `000-numbering-conventions/spec.md`; if not, classify it
>    as `project` (1500+) or, when `clients.json` declares an ecosystem parent/children, `ecosystem` (13xx–14xx).
> ## When you are a sub-agent

> above. Your prompt has `{{TASK}}` and `{{PROJECT_PATH}}` — use them as

Update `.ssot/status.md` and `.ssot/handoff.md`. Record completed work, exact current state, modified files, verification results, unresolved problems, next recommended action, and commands needed to resume. Separate facts from assumptions. Do not claim completion when required checks failed or were not run. Flag any unresolved questions that were researched but could not be resolved — include what was investigated and what remains unclear so the next session can pick up the research (rule 8).

**Project-specific verification (local-ai-packaged)**: this is an infrastructure project with
no test suite — do not report "tests passed" as a verification. Instead, run and record the
result of `docker compose config --quiet` (add the override files relevant to the session,
e.g. `-f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.minimal.yml`) before claiming a compose or
Dockerfile change is verified. If a container was touched, also record whether it was
restarted and observed healthy (`docker compose ps`), not merely that the config parses.

When the session involved a material decision between options, record the alternatives considered, their impacts, and why the chosen option was selected (decision-support rule) — this feeds the next cycle's C1 critique.

If the canonical context sources under `.ssot/agents/context/` (e.g., `AGENTS.src.md`, `CLAUDE.src.md`) were edited during the session, run `npx --no-install acos --fix` (or `maintenance.sync` / `0660-sync`) so the generated projections (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and client-specific pointers) are regenerated before handing off. Do not edit generated projections directly.

Run `npx --no-install acos --check` to confirm projections are in sync, then run
`npx --no-install acos-handoff-check --root .` to verify handoff/git consistency. Reconcile any
Git state/count contradiction before ending the session; do not edit the handoff automatically
merely to increase its score. Since spec 019 **E1**, the same check also verifies the
session bridge on a fresh handoff (`.ssot/next-session-prompt.md` + H1 artifact) —
run `1040-session-bridge` before this check or it will flag the gap.

After the handoff is written, check `.ssot/agents/dependencies.json`. If it exists, is valid JSON, and contains at least one dependency, invoke the `project.crosshandoff` entrypoint (`1080-cross-handoff`) to produce a cross-project handoff report for each declared downstream dependency. Include the resulting report in the session summary or attach it to the handoff.

If any entrypoint bodies were personalized during the session (via `1220-personalize` or manually), verify that the `personalized: true` marker is present in their frontmatter. This marker protects the entire customized entrypoint (body + frontmatter description) from being overwritten by `acos-migrate --reconcile --apply --refresh-bodies`. Note any newly personalized entrypoints in the handoff so the next session is aware.

## H1 — Next-cycle hypothesis (mandatory before 1040)

Spec: `../acos-mcp-launcher-work/docs/specs/019-cycle-continuity/spec.md` (invariant **H1**).

Before invoking `1040-session-bridge`, write (or refresh)
`.session/next-cycle-hypothesis.md`. Alias accepted during transition:
`.session/next-cycle-analysis.md` (same content requirements).

The hypothesis MUST include:

1. **Facts carried forward** — verified claims from this session (with command/result pointers).
2. **Open gaps** — each tagged `fact` | `hypothesis` | `ops-only`.
3. **Candidate lanes** — 1–5 next-cycle work items with intent, suggested wave role
   (`diagnose` | `fix` | `validate` | `ship`), write-set hint, parallelizable yes/no.
   Each lane MUST be **cycle-worthy**: a **significant** enrichment and/or
   problem-solving package for a full `1840` that uses the structured system
   (diagnose, C1, plan, G1, execute/waves, verify, tools) — not a chore that
   belongs in a normal chat turn. Micro-edits, one-file one-line tweaks,
   rename-only, “add a bullet”, and typo/comment-only fixes are **not** candidate
   lanes — put them in non-goals or handle them outside the cycle.
4. **Draft parallelizable task-plan base** — numbered tasks or wave/lane stubs with
   intended files/domains, dependencies, parallel vs sequential ownership. This is
   the seed the next fresh agent enriches then executes — not a vague leftover and
   not a locked rubber-stamp.
5. **Explicit non-goals** — what the next cycle must not redo or must not claim.
6. **Uncertainty log** — researched-but-unresolved questions for session N+1.

**Why:** end of cycle prepares the next cycle’s plan base; next session re-analyzes
with a fresh look, enriches, then executes — so the system’s power compounds.

Forbidden as the only next-action: a leftover sentence ("fix X") or an unstructured
shopping list. Ops-only items (push, deploy, bake) MUST be labeled `ops-only`.
Forbidden as sole (or primary) candidate lanes: hollow micro-tasks that burn a
cycle while leaving waves/audits/gates unused. If only trivial leftovers remain,
say so explicitly — do not invent a fake cycle around one tiny edit.

The handoff's "Next recommended action" MUST point at launching `1840-auto-improve` with
this hypothesis artifact (not a leftover sentence alone).

If this session ran an improve cycle (`1840` or equivalent) and H1 is missing, write it
now. Do **not** call `1040` until H1 exists.

## S1 — Next-cycle evidence scan (mandatory after improve cycles)

Spec: `../acos-mcp-launcher-work/docs/specs/019-cycle-continuity/spec.md` (invariant **S1**).
Cost rule: prefer direct reads over parallel subagents when coverage is enough
(see engine common.md §10 / frontier-plan-contract).

Before writing H1, gather live evidence instead of relying on session memory alone.
**Evidence is mandatory; parallel subagents are optional.**

Preferred order (stop when coverage is enough):

1. Direct reads / targeted shell for git state, harness check, known issues.
2. If gaps remain, dispatch up to 4 read-only sub-agents **in a single message**.
   Each writes `.session/next-cycle-scan/<lane>.md`:
   - `git-tests` — worktree state, ahead/behind; for this infra project record
     `docker compose config --quiet` (relevant override files), not a missing test suite
   - `docs-specs` — active specs vs implementation state, stale documentation
   - `harness` — `npx --no-install acos --check` result, drift, projection health
   - `risks` — open blockers, TODOs, known issues, uncertainty candidates
3. Sub-agents are read-only and re-orient independently per
   `.ssot/agents/context/orientation.md` → "When you are a sub-agent". They
   return compact findings, not prose.
4. H1's "Facts carried forward" and "Candidate lanes" MUST cite the evidence
   (scan artifacts and/or direct-read pointers).
5. After any `1840` (or equivalent) cycle the evidence scan is **mandatory**. For a
   trivial session (no improve cycle, small diff), the agent MAY record
   `scan: skipped — <reason>` in H1 instead.

After the handoff, cross-handoff, **S1**, and **H1** are complete, invoke
`1040-session-bridge` automatically to write `.ssot/next-session-prompt.md` and
deliver the copy-paste snippet for the next session (**B2**: persisted in the
prompt file, printed, and copied to the clipboard best-effort). This is
mandatory — every session handoff prepares the next session's auto-improve
cycle so the user only needs to paste the snippet at the start of the next
session. `acos-handoff-check` verifies both artifacts mechanically (**E1**) —
a handoff without them scores `review` at best.
